newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish child abuse priest jailed for 2-1/2 years.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish child abuse priest jailed for 2-1/2 years.

text.p: A Northern Irish Roman Catholic priest was sentenced to two-and-a-half years in prison on Friday for the sexual abuse of 10 young boys and girls in his care.
Father Joseph Michael Steele had pleaded guilty to 25 charges of indecently assaulting seven boys and three girls while working as a curate in Belfast between 1969 and 1983.
One of his victims was an eight-year-old altar boy and another a girl whom he sexually abused for three years while he coached her in gymnastics.

"Sexual abuse of children is a serious offence and it is particularly serious in your case because you enjoyed the trust of the children, their parents and the schools you worked for...you abused that trust," Judge John Martin told Steele as he sentenced him.
Steele's offences were uncovered when the sister of three of the children he abused discovered that he was working in the northern English county of Yorkshire.
His victims first confronted him and later informed police.
When he was questioned in court about the offences, Steele said he could not remember what he had done.
The plump, balding 56-year-old said his mind was a blur, but that his victims had no reason to lie. If they said he had abused them, he must have done so.
Steele's case is the latest in a string of sexual scandals involving Catholic priests in Northern Ireland. Church leaders have vowed to try to tackle the problem.
A spokesman for Steele's church said the priest had committed a "grave wrong" and offered sympathy to his victims and their families.
